comparator.name: Filosofie
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official Onderwijs- en Examenregeling bachelor Filosofie 2026-2027, using Appendix 2B for the full-time cohort starting in 2026-2027. The formal curriculum comprises two fixed 60-EC years followed by a 15-EC non-philosophy minor, 15 EC of Advanced Academic Skills choices, Filosofie in de Praktijk, one 7.5-EC philosophy elective and the 15-EC Bachelor Thesis. Where the current public study-programme page differs from the formal curriculum overview, the OER governs this reconstruction. The separate RASL double-study arrangement is not the normalized target reconstructed here, and the programme has no formal routes or specialisations requiring a route choice. The two Advanced Academic Skills slots take the first two of the three options in the order Appendix 2A lists them — Wittgenstein and Philosophies of Information and Computation — as a neutral tie-break fixed independently of the UCR side. The year-3 philosophy elective remains Contemporary Thought of Technology, a valid option in Appendix 2A that is also presented on the current public study-programme page. The 15-EC minor or exchange space is genuine non-philosophy profiling space and is preserved rather than filled with invented content.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is not a philosophy curriculum alone. It combines the five UCR philosophy courses and political philosophy with history, sociology, literary study, rhetoric, cognitive science and formal logic, because that is where UCR teaches the material a philosophy bachelor covers within its own discipline. The label therefore names both the philosophical core and the human-science fields through which the rest of that ground is reached, rather than presenting the programme as a full philosophy degree.

alternatives.concept: A programme organised around the philosophical and ethical evaluation of technology, information and artificial intelligence: the philosophical core is retained, and the elective space goes to media theory and to the technical study of the systems whose claims and effects are being assessed.

Philosophy of technology, information and artificial intelligence
alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum pairs the philosophical core with media study and with genuine technical work in data science, machine learning, deep learning and data management. The label names philosophy alongside the technology and media strands rather than describing the whole programme as philosophy of technology, since much of it is data science and media studies in their own right.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route drops the human-science strand — Modern History, Modern Sociology, Histories of Gender, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Higher Order Functions, Psycholinguistics, Introduction to Literary Studies, Style & Meaning, Modern Art & Modern Museums and Introduction to Political Philosophy — and replaces it with media archaeology, film and media analysis, platform media, media and race, documentary, and a technical sequence running from Introduction to Data Science through Machine Learning to Neural Networks & Deep Learning. The educational choice is different in kind: the student evaluates technology with working knowledge of how it is built, rather than studying mind and society through the human sciences. Ten of the 24 courses differ.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is an ethics programme grounded in actual environmental science, governance and engineering practice: climate science, life-cycle analysis, ecosystems, remediation, renewable design and sustainability governance sit alongside the philosophical core. The label states that combination rather than calling the programme philosophy of sustainability, which would overstate the philosophical share.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route keeps the ethical and political core but replaces the entire human-science and interpretive strand — Introduction to Literary Studies, Perspectives on Literary Meaning, Style & Meaning, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Higher Order Functions, Psycholinguistics, Philosophy of Mind, AI Ethics, Modern History, Histories of Gender, Modern Art & Modern Museums and Logic & Discrete Mathematics — with the two sustainability gateways, climate science, life-cycle analysis, ecosystems, remediation, renewable system design, sustainability governance, environmental justice, climate communication and delta research. Compared with the technology route it shares only the philosophical core and the method courses. The student here argues about environmental obligations from inside the technical and governance practice being judged. Twelve of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and fourteen from the technology route.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Introduction to Western Philosophy, Introduction to Political Philosophy and Introduction to Literary Studies open the programme and precede all later philosophical, political and interpretive work. Introduction to Brain & Behavior is taken in semester 2 and is the formal prerequisite for Higher Order Functions in semester 5 and Psycholinguistics in semester 6. Introduction to Literary Studies precedes Perspectives on Literary Meaning, which explicitly applies theoretical perspectives to texts. Modern Sociology in semester 3 precedes the advanced interpretive and historical work of year 3. Ethics and Philosophy of Mind at 200 level precede Philosophy of Emotion and Free Will, Time & the Self at 300 level, which build on them conceptually. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the twelve generator-eligible interests that describe philosophy as a discipline — fundamental questions, truth and knowledge, what it is to be human, critical and logical thinking, argument, close reading, the history of ideas, contemporary philosophy in public debate, justice, the analytic and continental traditions, existential questions and the good life. The two remaining generator-eligible interests each define a coherent direction of its own: the philosophy of technology together with philosophy across medicine, AI and economics, and sustainability and environmental ethics. Both are supported by named components of the current official curriculum — Philosophy of Art, Media & Technology, Contemporary Thought of Technology and the information-and-communication Advanced Academic Skills course for the first; Moral Philosophy and Environmental Practice for the second — and both can be built as valid UCR programmes that differ from the closest match and from each other by well over the four-course floor. Three alternatives are therefore included and the maximum is reached; no further candidate direction was constructed, since every remaining interest row is either a curricular topic supporting these three concepts or a search-only outcome row.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Inleiding Filosofie corresponds to Introduction to Western Philosophy.

Human Conditions and Philosophy of Mind both take the philosophical analysis of what it is to be human as their primary subject: consciousness, personal identity and the limits of naturalistic explanation.

Both are the systematic moral-philosophy component of their programme. UCR's Ethics works through theories of moral reasoning and virtue ethics using climate change, future generations and animal ethics as its applied material, which is the same combination of moral theory and environmental practice.

Both are the advanced metaphysics component. Free Will, Time & the Self treats freedom, time, agency and selfhood, though analytically rather than through the continental tradition the Rotterdam course follows.

Contemporary Thought of Technology and AI Ethics both examine technology philosophically. UCR's course concentrates that examination on artificial intelligence, fairness, alignment and human flourishing.

Theoretical Analytic Philosophy is a dedicated survey of analytic method and its central problems. No single UCR course occupies that role; the material is spread across Philosophy of Mind, Free Will, Time & the Self and Logic & Discrete Mathematics, so the component is left unmatched rather than forced onto one of them.

What Can We Know? is a systematic epistemology course running from antiquity to the modern age. UCR offers no epistemology course, and Introduction to Western Philosophy — which touches these questions — is the counterpart of the Rotterdam introduction rather than of this one.
Filosofie in Nederland studies the Dutch philosophical tradition specifically. UCR has no counterpart and none is manufactured.

Logica en Formele Filosofie and Logic & Discrete Mathematics are both the formal-logic component, covering propositional and predicate structure and formal reasoning; the UCR course adds discrete mathematics and applications to computing.

Philosophy of Science is a dedicated course on scientific knowledge, method and explanation. UCR has no philosophy-of-science course. Calling Bullshit trains the evaluation of evidence and scientific credibility but is a critical-thinking course rather than a philosophical treatment of science, so the component is left unmatched.

Filosofie in de Praktijk places philosophical skills in professional practice. UCR's Personal & Professional Development serves a different purpose — personal formation and academic-skills development, without the disciplinary content — so the component is recorded as unmatched rather than equated with it.

Historisering van het Wereldbeeld and Modern History both study how worldviews were historically formed and transformed; the UCR course does so through the political and intellectual history of the modern period from 1815.
Geschiedenis, Maatschappij en Individu and Modern Sociology both examine the relation between society and the individual through social theory and the history of modernity.
Het Lichaam: tussen Ervaring, Discours en Macht and Histories of Gender both study the body as lived experience shaped by discourse and power, approached through gender.

Politics and Critique and Introduction to Political Philosophy are both the programme's political-philosophy component, examining political authority, society and critique through influential thinkers.

Enlightenment is a dedicated study of Enlightenment philosophy. Modern History begins in 1815 and is already the counterpart of Historisering van het Wereldbeeld, so no UCR course covers this period philosophically and the gap is preserved.

Taal en Geest and Psycholinguistics both address the relation between language and mind. The Rotterdam course does so philosophically and the UCR course through the neurobiological and psychological study of language acquisition, production and comprehension; the primary subject is the same.

Wittgenstein is a dedicated advanced seminar on one philosopher and his work on language, logic and meaning. UCR addresses some related questions in broader philosophy and language courses but offers no dedicated Wittgenstein or philosophy-of-language course, so the component remains unmatched.

Philosophy of Art, Media & Technology and Introduction to Film & Media share art, media and technology as their subject, including how media technologies shape perception and cultural production; the UCR course is an analytical rather than a philosophical treatment.

Philosophies of Information and Computation treats information and computation as philosophical subjects. UCR offers technical computing, formal logic and AI-ethics courses, but none centres on the philosophy of information and computation, so the component remains unmatched rather than being equated with applied technical study.

The Rotterdam programme reserves 15 EC of genuine non-philosophy profiling space as a minor or exchange period. UCR programmes are composed entirely of 7.5-EC courses and have no equivalent reserved block, so the space is shown as it stands.
The Bachelor Thesis Filosofie is a 15-EC supervised independent philosophical study. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so the component is recorded as unmatched.

notes.text: The Rotterdam programme is a full philosophy curriculum: a systematic sequence in the history of philosophy, epistemology, metaphysics, logic, philosophy of science, philosophy of language and mind, moral and political philosophy, closing with a 15-EC philosophical thesis. UCR teaches five philosophy courses — Introduction to Western Philosophy, Ethics, Philosophy of Mind, Philosophy of Emotion, and Free Will, Time & the Self — together with Introduction to Political Philosophy, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy and AI Ethics. At UCR the remaining philosophical ground is approached through neighbouring fields: the history of ideas through history, social critique through sociology, interpretation through literary study and rhetoric, and mind and language through cognitive science. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives on philosophical questions rather than reproducing a full philosophy curriculum, and UCR has no dedicated epistemology, philosophy of science or single-philosopher course.
